articles.title: Hackers Used Meta’s AI Support Bot to Seize Instagram Accounts
articles.summary: Microsoft drops a record-breaking 200 patches this Patch Tuesday, with nearly three dozen rated 'critical' — because apparently Redmond's security team had a particularly productive month discovering their own mistakes.

articles.title: Victory! 702 has Expired!
articles.summary: CISA contractor accidentally dumps AWS GovCloud keys and agency secrets on GitHub, proving that even the cybersecurity agency can't secure its own contractors. Congress is predictably losing its collective mind.

articles.title: Yes to California's Bill to Ban Surveillance Pricing
articles.summary: Section 702 surveillance authority finally expires, marking a rare victory against the NSA's warrantless dragnet. Time to pop champagne before they inevitably find another loophole.

articles.title: Claude Fable 5 Doesn't Change the Mythos Security Story
articles.summary: ShinyHunters exploits Oracle ERP zero-day to rampage through American universities, proving that higher education's IT security is about as robust as their student loan forgiveness programs.

articles.title: ICE Should Show It Hasn’t Been “Infiltrated by Violent Extremists,” Senator Urges
articles.summary: Indiana bans press from executions under the guise of 'dignity,' but really it's just good old-fashioned state repression. Nothing says transparency like murdering people in secret.

articles.title: Critical Splunk Enterprise Flaw Lets Attackers Run Code Without Authentication
articles.summary: Palo Alto confirms active exploitation of GlobalProtect VPN authentication bypass flaw. When your VPN security company can't secure VPNs, maybe it's time to reconsider the whole cybersecurity industrial complex.

articles.title: Week in review: Exploited Check Point VPN zero-day, Oracle PeopleSoft servers under attack
articles.summary: Critical Splunk Enterprise flaw allows unauthenticated remote code execution with a perfect 9.8 CVSS score. Your log analysis tool just became someone else's favorite backdoor.

articles.title: Oracle warns of security bug that hackers abused to breach 100+ companies | TechCrunch
articles.summary: 23andMe settles data breach lawsuit for $46.75M after hackers accessed genetic data of millions. Your DNA profile is now worth approximately $2.50 in settlement money.

articles.title: Oracle Addresses PeopleSoft Vulnerability Amid Reports of Zero-Day Attacks
articles.summary: Oracle warns of security bug exploited by cybercrime gangs to breach 100+ companies in mass-hacking campaign. Larry Ellison's empire continues its tradition of being a hacker's best friend.

articles.title: CISA BOD 26-04: Frequently asked questions about the new risk-based patching directive
articles.summary: Oracle addresses PeopleSoft zero-day amid ShinyHunters attacks, but won't confirm if it's actually the exploited vulnerability. Classic Oracle transparency — about as clear as their licensing agreements.
